description: Mechanically checkable subset of voices/john.md. Built from five samples (~70,900 words) of published review-essay prose; every count below is measured there. Judgment rules stay in the markdown.

engine_exemptions.chatbot-artifact: attested conversational style ('of course,' / 'certainly,' connective in review-essays)

banned_regex.label: Hype-register adjectives
banned_regex.example: The tool's seamless integration has been game-changing for the whole team.
banned_regex.note: Zero occurrences across 70,893 words. The samples praise and pan in plain words and star ratings, never in launch-note adjectives.

banned_regex.label: Committee hedge
banned_regex.rx: (?i)\b(it could be argued|one might argue|it is (?:widely )?believed that)\b
banned_regex.example: It could be argued that the policy helped consumers.
banned_regex.note: Opinions in this voice are owned in the first person, including the uncertain ones: 'I think', 'I suppose', 'I don't know'.

signature_moves.label: Explicit star-rating verdict
signature_moves.note: The review-essay close: 'I give X four and a half stars.' One per piece, after the turn. Two is already a callback; three is a tic.

signature_moves.label: 'of course' as connective
signature_moves.note: Genuine habit (37 in 70,893 words, 0.52/1k), listed with a ceiling rather than a floor so a conversion cannot carpet a draft with it. The engine's chatbot lexicon flags this phrase at P0; over this writer it is a false positive.

contrastive_pairs.would: But luck decided most of it.
contrastive_pairs.would_never: However, it is important to note that luck decided most of it.

contrastive_pairs.would: I give hotel breakfasts three stars.
contrastive_pairs.would_never: In conclusion, hotel breakfasts merit a rating of three stars.

contrastive_pairs.would: We used a lot of it.
contrastive_pairs.would_never: We utilized a sufficient quantity of it.
